findings.desc: README still documents the old B-c25c exact-budget approval gate after B-6529 replaced it with a frozen Cell 03 execution envelope and postflight provider-reported usage accounting. At experiments/multi-model-ablation/README.md:16-18 and :228 it still says m2-provider-execution-launch has missing metadata blockers, the Cell 03 guardrail has exact spend approval absent, amount/currency/approvalSource/approvedBy/approvalDate are required before spend, and the checker validates invented/unbound budget approval. The current implementation forbids old exact-budget gate keys and validates preRunDollarGuessRequired=false / preRunDollarCapAsSoleGateAllowed=false instead, so the README gives stale launch semantics to future operators.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 4d924276d16a936759ff4e9025c0d09ebaf72889. README no longer describes the old exact-budget approval gate; it now states frozen Cell 03 execution envelope, pre-run dollar guess not required, provider calls disabled in this authorization story, postflight provider-reported usage/cost accounting required after future execution, and Cell 06 blocked until real Cell 03-derived budget/usage lock. Verified by m2-provider-execution-check and m2-launch-readiness-check.

findings.desc: m2-provider-execution-check.mjs loads m2-provider-execution-authorization.json but never validates it: providerAuthorization is returned from loadArtifacts() at lines 636-638, yet validateAll() only checks providerLaunch, Cell 03 guardrail/envelope, policies, tool surface, runner manifest, readiness, and status at lines 583-625. README line 232 promises the checker records/validates the B-11be metadata authorization with USD 0.00 spend. As written, mutations to m2-provider-execution-authorization.json authorizationBoundary, provider spend, required metadata blockers, or sequencing would not fail the provider execution check, leaving a silent coverage hole for the full B-6529 change.
